text:
tara: Heads-up: 99p latency spike observed on shared pool 'v2-shared' starting ~03:42 UTC. 99p jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s across multiple hosts :eyes:

samir: saw this in the dashboards too. any recent deploys?

li: there was a canary kernel heuristic flip at 03:40 that enables 'adaptive prefetch' on medium/large batches. rolling canary -> 10% of traffic. i can check which tenants hit the canary.

tara: timeline aligns. can you paste the deploy id?

li: deploy id rk-kernel-2026-03-18-428, rolled at 03:40:12.

nate: quick probe: `rkctl perf tail --pool v2-shared --metric latency_99 --since 03:30` shows sharp step at 03:42. also saw per-tenant 99p diverge — a few tenants get >2s while most are back to ~300ms.

benchie: running a targeted load repro against tenant T-482 now to validate. small-batch traffic seems unaffected, long-seq and mix-batch workloads blow up.

li: hypothesis: adaptive prefetch increases kernel memory reads that collide with KV cache eviction patterns for long-seq requests, causing tail latency for tenants with larger token windows.

samir: can we confirm KV cache hit-rate change? grab `kv_hit_rate_5m` per-tenant around the window.

li: pasted sample from metrics (simplified):
```
tenant T-482: kv_hit_rate 86% -> 58% at 03:42
tenant T-199: kv_hit_rate 92% -> 90%
tenant T-513: kv_hit_rate 79% -> 45%
pool avg: 90% -> 72%
```

tara: that's bad. eviction wave + prefetch causing extra memory bandwidth and forcing more kernel fallbacks?

nate: I profiled one host with `perf` and our runtime logs. the trace shows `kernel:prefetch_read()` calls spike and memory stalls increase 3x. Also observed more frequent kernel switches (quant-path -> fp16-path) around the same time.

benchie: repro results: with adaptive prefetch enabled 99p=1.1s, rollback to previous kernel heuristic 99p=210ms. baseline stable.

opsbot: deploy-bot: rollback triggered for rk-kernel-2026-03-18-428 by tara at 04:05:18 UTC.

li: rollback done. still collecting metrics but early signs look good.

samir: good. we need a short mitigation plan and follow-up. suggestions:
- add KV-aware guard to prefetch (do not prefetch when per-tenant kv_hit_rate < 80%)
- add a soft per-tenant long-seq cap in shared pool (concurrency/slots for sequences > 1024)
- add telemetry: prefetch_count per-tenant + kernel_prefetch_evictions

tara: agree. immediate actions: 1) revert permanent until guard is implemented (done). 2) add kpm alert for prefetch-induced eviction waves. 3) add e2e perf test in canary that includes long-seq KV-heavy workload.

li: i'll open a PR with the KV-guard flag and unit tests today. also adding a flag to limit prefetch aggressiveness by tenant-score.

nate: i'll add a short sampling profiler job to run on canary hosts during kernel changes (30m sample) and dump a flamegraph to S3 for quick triage.

benchie: will run a batch of regression tests overnight: small/medium/long sequences with mixed kernels. will post run summary in this thread.

tara: postmortem owners: li (cause + fix), nate (profiling + telemetry), benchie (repros + test coverage). we'll sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

samir: one more ask: add a simple per-tenant KV hit-rate heatmap to the console so paging on noisy tenants is easier.

li: ack. creating follow-ups. thanks all for quick response :thumbsup:

benchie: quick update 07:20 UTC: nightly regressions finished, prefetch-guard branch passed long-seq scenarios locally, no perf regression on small-batch. will PR this morning.

tara: closing loop when PR merged and new canary run looks clean. saved the traces and logs under s3://redwood-perf/repro/1719009876-prefetch-sweep/

opsbot: incident-bot: incident classified as Sev-2 (temporary rollback, customer impact on a small subset). incident-incident-1719009876 created.

samir: nice work. leaving notes for product/ssrm to reach out to top impacted tenants for transparency.
